entries.title: Activate a Microsoft Marketplace purchase
entries.summary: Where a Microsoft Marketplace buyer lands after purchasing a three.ws plan: sign in with Microsoft Entra ID to link the subscription to a three.ws account and switch the plan on.

entries.title: Add three.ws to ChatGPT: free 3D models and avatars inside your chats
entries.summary: Add the free three.ws 3D Studio to your own ChatGPT in about a minute: the exact settings to paste, a live check of the server from your browser, prompts to try and fixes for every setup snag. Text and photos become interactive 3D models and rigged avatars inline in the conversation. No account, no key.

entries.title: Connect to every three.ws tool
entries.summary: One MCP endpoint and one sign-in for every three.ws tool. Copy-paste config for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and the @three-ws/mcp stdio proxy, with the live tool count and tool groups read from the same registry the endpoint serves.

entries.title: Docs · Account deletion and the 30-day purge
entries.summary: What happens after you delete a three.ws account: the 30-day recovery window, the permanent purge of uploads and account data, the records kept for legal and accounting reasons and how they are stripped of your identity, and the hashed receipt each purge leaves.

entries.title: Docs · MCP integrations
entries.summary: How an agent connects third-party MCP servers: the catalog, OAuth and token sign-in, tool tiers and acknowledgements, custom-server review, the HTTP API, the three-ws mcp install CLI, and how to add a server to the catalog.

entries.title: Docs · Microsoft distribution and offer plan
entries.summary: How three.ws turns its live Microsoft Marketplace publisher profile into offers: a transactable SaaS listing, Copilot MCP certification, professional services, a Power Platform connector, a Teams app, and the VS Code and Edge stores.

entries.title: Docs · Microsoft Marketplace SaaS offer
entries.summary: How a Microsoft Marketplace purchase becomes a three.ws plan: the landing page, Entra sign-in, the fulfilment webhook, hourly metered billing and its retry rules, the env vars, and how to test against a preview offer.

entries.title: Docs · Partner shoutout playbook
entries.summary: How three.ws earns public mentions from partners and prospective partners: give real value first, make the post a byproduct, and never sell credit for a post.

entries.title: Docs · three-ws-agent
entries.summary: Run a three.ws agent in your terminal: a streaming TUI with slash commands and per-class tool approvals, searchable sessions, parallel subagents, plain-language cron that runs locally or as a three.ws automation, and a Telegram gateway for allowlisted chats.

entries.title: Docs · World chat in /play: scrollback and the community board
entries.summary: How a late joiner sees a /play world's last 60 chat lines above a caught-up divider, the cap, expiry and privacy rules for stored lines, and the read-only Board tab that shows a coin's community posts in-world.

entries.title: MCP Integrations
entries.summary: Connect your agent to third-party MCP servers: a vetted catalog of 80+ servers (documentation, developer tools, project trackers, CRM, payments, data and more) plus any public HTTPS server by URL. Sign in with OAuth or paste a token, turn tools on per agent grouped by read, write and financial tiers, and review a custom server's tools before anything runs. The agent sees each tool as ext_<name>_<tool>.

entries.title: MCP Tool Access Settings
entries.summary: Choose which three.ws MCP tool groups your agents, connectors and AI clients can call. Turn a group on to unlock its financial tools such as swaps, transfers and launches, or off to hide it everywhere. Every disabled-tool refusal links here.

entries.title: three.ws agents (Microsoft Teams tab)
entries.summary: The three.ws tab inside Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365: pick one of your agents and talk to it, or generate a 3D model from a prompt, without leaving the meeting or chat.

entries.title: $THREE purchases and Premium pass payments build correctly for the Token-2022 mint
entries.summary: $THREE is a Token-2022 token, and several Solana payment builders were deriving token accounts under the older token program, which produces a transfer the network rejects. Skill purchases, agent purchases, subscriptions and the Premium data pass now read the token program from the mint and create any missing $THREE account in the same transaction. A new script simulates both the gasless purchase and the Premium payment for a real holder on mainnet without signing or sending anything, and both pass.

entries.title: 3D generation workers accept PNG, JPEG and WEBP only, and say so when an image is refused
entries.summary: Every photo you hand Forge, avatar reconstruction or scene decomposition is now decoded only as PNG, JPEG or WEBP, so a file in any other format never reaches an image parser on the GPU workers. A refused or corrupt image now fails with a clear message naming the three formats instead of a generic worker error. The image library is pinned exactly on every worker, the talking-avatar worker moves to transformers 4.57.6 with bit-identical output, and oversized EXIF blocks are ignored rather than parsed. Takes effect as each worker image is rebuilt.

entries.title: A paid agent skill call whose response was lost can now be collected again without paying twice
entries.summary: When you pay for an agent skill and the connection drops before the answer arrives, asking again with the same Idempotency-Key (or the same payment intent) now returns the stored result, marked replayed, instead of a payment_in_flight error or a second charge. The skill runs once and the author is credited once. A retry with different arguments is refused with idempotency_conflict, a retry while the first call is still running gets idempotency_in_progress with a retry-after, and a call that fails stores nothing so the paid intent can be retried. The 402 challenge and the manifest now advertise the header, the 24 hour window and the replayed field, and the browser x402 client sends one key per call and retries a dropped paid request once on its own.

entries.title: Add three.ws to your own ChatGPT in about a minute
entries.summary: A new /chatgpt page walks you through adding the free three.ws 3D Studio to ChatGPT: turn on developer mode, create an app with the URL https://three.ws/api/mcp-chatgpt and no authentication, then ask for a model. Text and photos become interactive, textured 3D models and rigged avatars that render inline in the conversation, free and with no account. The page checks the server live from your browser, lists the exact tools ChatGPT gets, and has starter prompts and fixes for every setup snag.

entries.title: Agent payment mandates are pinned to USDC and refuse any other currency
entries.summary: An Intent Mandate lets your agent pay other agents without asking you each time, within a budget. Issuing one with an empty or non-USDC currency used to succeed and quietly turned off the currency check, so a payment in an asset the spend guard cannot price could bypass your per-payment, daily and per-recipient dollar limits. Mandates now accept USDC only, refuse anything else with unsupported_currency, and any mandate signed with a bad currency before this fix is refused when the agent tries to spend under it.

entries.title: Agent wallet key export and rotation now require the real-funds agreements
entries.summary: Exporting an agent wallet key and confirming a rotate-and-sweep now check that the owner has signed the real-funds agreements, like every other path that moves or releases custodial funds. The rotation preview stays open, devnet is unaffected, and an owner who has not signed can sign and retry with the same re-authentication. Agent wallet provisioning also claims the wallet slot atomically, so two concurrent first requests can no longer replace a key whose address was already handed out.

entries.title: Agents on one stage take turns speaking instead of talking over each other
entries.summary: When several <agent-3d> agents share an <agent-stage>, everything they say out loud now goes through one speaking queue, so a cue answered by two agents plays one voice after the other. Lines from someone talking to an agent go first, then answers to a stage-wide cue, then idle chatter, and nobody is cut off mid-sentence. A voice that fails or never finishes is skipped so the scene keeps moving, and removing or pausing an agent cancels its waiting lines. Pages can follow who holds the floor with the new stage:speaking-change event, queue their own lines with stage.speak(), and say() now resolves to the reply. Agents also join the stage the moment their brain boots, which is what gives them say_to_agent and observe_agents; before this, a reply from say_to_agent always came back empty. The two-agents example shows the floor live.

entries.title: Agents SDK routes are all real
entries.summary: Every @three-ws/agents method now calls a mounted /api/v1 route: account usage, budget, ledger, integrations and link codes, six market intel reads (price, top movers, RSI/EMA/MACD indicators, signals, anomalies, macro) and read-only agent wallet balance and history. Swap execution and transfers stay out of the API by design. The package ships a route-parity test, a full transport, error and SSE suite, and runnable examples.

entries.title: Announced surfaces defect sweep
entries.summary: Fixed a batch of rough edges on recently announced pages: the Herald avatar presenter now holds its full dwell and honors reduced motion, the validation report renders again, Labs sorts unmatched experiments into Other, the /3d live badge is restructured, the inspector measures quantized and meshopt models correctly, the stream demo reports a faster, about the same or slower first frame honestly, and the avatar-stream package declares its dependencies. Docs now say the talking-avatar video worker is not yet deployed.

entries.title: Autonomous agent runs can use the integrations you connected
entries.summary: A run you start from the API or the Runs tab can now call the third-party MCP servers you connected to the agent on /mcp-integrations, the same ext_ tools chat already had. Every call shows on the Runs tab with its arguments, the server's answer and the step's cost. Tools that move money or cannot be undone stay out of autonomous runs, since nobody is there to approve them; the agent says in its report that you need to take that step. A run's toolsAllowed list can now name ext_ tools too.

entries.title: Catalog and reconstructed avatars load again in embeds and the walk companion
entries.summary: Avatars whose model lives outside the main bucket, such as the built-in catalog characters and avatars rebuilt from a photo, answered 404 on their embed-friendly GLB link, so embeds and the walk companion showed the robot placeholder instead. That link now serves those models, with the same open cross-origin access as every other avatar.

entries.title: Chain turnover never reads as zero, and coin signals say why they are blank
entries.summary: On /chains, a chain whose 24h DEX volume is tiny next to its TVL now shows <0.001x instead of 0.000x, which looked like no trading at all, and the Turnover header's info icon is drawn so it no longer shows as an empty box on systems without that character. On a coin's launch page, the "Seeded by one funder" and "Launch tx" cells still show a dash when the signal cannot be computed, but hovering now tells you why, for example when a coin has too much trade history to reach its creation transaction.

entries.title: Characters and Rankings now show real creators only
entries.summary: Accounts our own QA and end-to-end sweeps sign up were showing on /characters and /rankings as if they were creators, including dozens of "QA squad" agents. Those accounts are now marked as test accounts, from signup onward, and both boards leave them out, so ranks stay contiguous and every card belongs to a real person. Character cards also no longer show an agent wallet's dollar balance; the address chip is still there.

entries.title: Connect your agent to third-party MCP servers
entries.summary: The new MCP Integrations page connects an agent to GitHub, Linear, Notion, DeepWiki and 80+ other vetted MCP servers, or any public HTTPS MCP server by URL. Sign in with OAuth or paste a token, then choose which tools the agent may call: read tools start on, write and financial tools stay off until you acknowledge each one, and a custom server's tools are reviewed before anything runs. The agent sees them as ext_ tools in every run, and the same connections can be made from the CLI with three-ws mcp install.

entries.title: Deleted accounts are now permanently purged after 30 days
entries.summary: The privacy policy promises that a deleted account is kept for 30 days for recovery and then permanently purged. A daily job now does that purge: your uploads are removed from storage and your account data is deleted. Records the law requires us to keep, such as payment history and your acceptance of the Terms, stay but no longer link to you or show your wallet or email. If a marketplace bid or sale involving your agent is still settling, the purge waits until the other person has been paid or refunded. During the 30 days, signing in with the same wallet says the account was deleted; after the purge, that wallet can start a fresh account.

entries.title: Embeds can allowlist the skill authors and hosts they trust
entries.summary: The agent-3d element's whitelist skill policy now works: list the authors you trust with skill-trusted-authors and the hosts with skill-trusted-origins (or set el.skillTrust from script), and only skills from those authors or hosts install. Before this, whitelist mode had no way to receive the lists and refused every skill. A refused skill now fires a skill:error event so the page can tell the visitor, and a misspelled skill-trust value falls back to the safe owner-only default instead of installing everything unchecked.

entries.title: Every new agent now starts with a drafted coin
entries.summary: A new agent gets a private coin plan drafted from its own name and persona, and its Solana wallet is set up at creation if that step had failed. Owners see a Next step card on the agent page with the drafted name and ticker, whether the launch wallet can cover launch costs, and one Review and launch button that opens the confirmation screen, where nothing is signed or spent until you approve it. Each step from plan viewed to launch succeeded is now recorded so the launch drop-off can be measured.

entries.title: Every page of the docs re-checked against the code it describes
entries.summary: All 158 docs that had fallen behind the code were reread against the changes that moved under them. 123 were corrected (endpoints, defaults, counts, limits, file paths, and features that have since shipped), 21 were confirmed still accurate, and 14 dated records such as event write-ups were marked as historical so they are no longer flagged. The freshness check now tracks each review, and its allowed stale count drops from 121 to 13, so drift shows up as soon as code changes.

entries.title: Every platform fee now has its own ledger, and bundle and subscription earnings are booked correctly
entries.summary: Each fee three.ws takes (pump.fun trades and launches, agent trades, skill sales, bundles, subscriptions and the x402 skill split) is now recorded once in an append-only fee ledger, in the same database write as the purchase or trade it belongs to, and replays never record it twice. A daily reconciler checks every recorded fee against what the fee wallet actually received on Solana. Bundle and subscription confirmations also stopped booking a platform fee when the buyer paid the full price straight to the creator, so creators now see their full earnings for those sales.

entries.title: Grok Bot gets the Solana market, and three.ws events can wake it
entries.summary: The three.ws connector for Grok Bot now covers more than 3D. Signed in, Grok can read live pump.fun graduations and token intel, Oracle conviction plays, the Sentiment Scout, token due diligence, the trader leaderboard and Solana agent passports, and a new market-brief prompt turns them into a scheduled daily brief. None of these tools can trade or spend. Developer webhooks can now carry a bearer token, so a three.ws event such as a finished generation or agent run can start a Grok Bot routine. The token is stored encrypted and never shown again. The /grok page and docs also cover Grok Build, xAI's coding CLI, which picks up the three.ws MCP config and plugin marketplace with no extra setup.

entries.title: Health checks now show when the Granite Guardian governance model is not serving
entries.summary: Granite Guardian screens agent messages, identities and autonomous sends for risks like jailbreaks and harm. When no Guardian lane was configured, the assess endpoint answered 503 and the identity check let everything through, yet every health probe stayed green. /api/healthz now carries a granite_guardian subsystem: down in production while no lane is set, ok once the self-hosted GPU worker answers its health probe or the watsonx lane is configured, and degraded when the self-hosted worker fails but watsonx can still answer. The worker deploy config was also corrected for the pinned vLLM release, which no longer accepts one of its old flags.

entries.title: Hover tips no longer swallow the click on the button underneath
entries.summary: A hover tip that opened over a neighbouring control used to catch the click meant for it, and stayed open while the pointer sat on it. On /render-lab the Contact sheet tip covered the Poses button, so clicking Poses did nothing. Plain hover tips now let clicks pass straight through and close the moment you press their control. Glossary term tips keep their Full glossary link reachable while they are showing.

entries.title: HumanIK avatars and complete bodies without finger joints now animate
entries.summary: Two kinds of avatar used to pass every check and then stand still in their bind pose. HumanIK and MotionBuilder rigs name their joints Character1:Hips, which three.js turns into Character1Hips when it loads the model, and that spelling mapped to nothing. Both spellings now resolve, and so does Character1_LeftArm. A complete body with no finger joints, such as a Meshy biped or a handless Mixamo export, fell under the clip coverage floor because 30 of a clip's 53 tracks are fingers; clips now bind when half of either all tracks or the 23 body tracks map, so fingers are optional and the shipped half-body avatar keeps animating. The live viewer, Rig Doctor, avatar thumbnails and the avatar capabilities API now all ask one gate, so a rig cannot be called animatable on one surface and fail on another. Across uploaded avatars in production, 333 of 350 skinned rigs now animate, up from 306.

entries.title: Install three.ws for Home Assistant through HACS
entries.summary: The three.ws Home Assistant integration now has its own public repository, github.com/nirholas/three-ws-home-assistant, with a 1.0.2 release. In HACS, add it under Custom repositories (category Integration), install three.ws, restart, and paste the pairing code from three.ws/smart-home. Your house opens one outgoing connection, nothing on your network is exposed, and no Home Assistant token ever leaves the house. It passes the real HACS and hassfest validation checks, ships its own brand icon, and is listed under AI and voice assistants. A HACS default-store listing, which removes the custom repository step, is prepared.

entries.title: Invite friends to a /play world with a QR code and a link that unfurls as that coin
entries.summary: A new Invite button in /play (and on every lobby card) opens a sheet with a live QR code, the world's link with one-click Copy, and Share, falling back to X and Telegram where the browser has no share sheet. During the week before an event and while it is live, the sheet leads with the event name and a countdown. Pasted links now unfurl as the coin's own world: its art, ticker, name and the biome it actually renders in, instead of a generic Play card. The card also used to name the wrong biome for most coins and showed no art for $THREE; both are fixed.

entries.title: Join a /play world late and catch up on what was said
entries.summary: Walking into a world mid-conversation no longer means an empty chat box. You now see the last 60 lines, stamped with when they were said, above a "You're caught up" divider, and new lines carry on below it. Reconnecting or refreshing never repeats a line, screen readers hear one short summary instead of the whole backlog, and an empty world offers a Say hi button. Lines are kept for at most three days and only name, text and time are stored. Worlds can also show the coin's community board in a read-only Board tab next to world chat.

entries.title: Knocks, agent mail and event markets get their own tabs on /notifications
entries.summary: The notifications page now builds its filter tabs from the same category list as your notification preferences, so it can no longer fall out of step with them. Knocks, agent mail, event-market entries, orders and approvals each get their own tab instead of landing under Account, and those rows now read as sentences ("Scout got mail from Bob") with their own icon. A knock now opens your knock inbox when clicked. Only categories you have notifications in are shown, the tabs work with arrow keys, each empty tab links to that category's delivery settings, and if the category list cannot load the page still shows everything with a Retry.

entries.title: Large 3D generations stop dropping mid-job, and photo cutouts move to a commercially licensed model
entries.summary: Very detailed TRELLIS generations could stall the worker long enough for Cloud Run to restart it, so every job on that machine failed with a malformed response. The worker now keeps each bake within a measured face budget, which covers every model that already succeeded. The TripoSG photo lane cuts out your subject with BiRefNet through our own background-removal service instead of a non-commercial model. Image lanes move to Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, falling back to the previous model only where the new one is not served. The scan page now says plainly that generating needs a free account.

entries.title: Live agent screens can no longer be steered into internal addresses
entries.summary: The browser behind an agent's live screen, the one an owner can take the wheel of, now enforces its address guard on every connection instead of only on the URL typed in. All of its traffic goes through a guard that looks up each hostname, refuses anything that lands on a loopback, private, link-local or cloud metadata address, and connects only to the address it checked. A public page that redirects to an internal host, an image or websocket pointed at one, or a name that resolves to one is now refused, so nothing internal can ever show up on the public wall.

entries.title: Make a $THREE holders-only embed from Widget Studio, no code needed
entries.summary: Widget Studio has a new Holders only panel. Pick one of your own avatars, flip the switch, set how much $THREE a viewer must hold (or click a holder tier, converted to tokens at the live price), and copy a snippet that only renders the 3D avatar for wallets that clear the bar. Every load checks the real balance on Solana. The panel reads the gate back from the server every time you pick the avatar, so it always shows what the embed enforces. From there you can change the requirement or remove the gate. Another Solana token can be used from the advanced field.

entries.title: NVIDIA Inception startups can apply for free generation credit, and earn more for a shoutout
entries.summary: If your startup is in NVIDIA Inception, the NVIDIA page now has a short application for $25 of prepaid credit, usable on the high-quality, game-ready, rigging and motion lanes. Once approved you can post about what you made on X or LinkedIn, paste the link, and earn $10 more after we confirm the post is public. The free text-to-3D lane is unchanged and still needs no account. NVIDIA has no way to verify membership, so a person checks each application and each post. Goes live with the next owner-approved deploy, after its database migration is applied.

entries.title: One MCP server for every three.ws tool: https://three.ws/mcp
entries.summary: https://three.ws/mcp (also /api/mcp/all) now mounts every tool from every hosted three.ws MCP server behind one URL and one sign-in, 371 tools in 19 groups, each tool classed as read, write or financial. A key or session sees the read and write tiers by default and turns financial groups on explicitly, and every call keeps the scope checks, rate limits and x402 pricing of the server it came from. The seven older endpoints work unchanged. Open /mcp in a browser for the live tool and group counts and copy-paste install steps for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and any stdio client; the new @three-ws/mcp package is the stdio proxy for clients that cannot speak HTTP. npm run check:mcp-tools now fails the gate if two servers publish the same name or a tool has no group or tier.

entries.title: Opening the spin wheel no longer drops everyone in the world
entries.summary: Opening the spin wheel in /play could crash the game server and disconnect every player in the world at once. The wheel now opens normally, and when paid spins are unavailable it says so instead of failing. The server also stays up through any single bad message from one player, so one fault costs that player one action rather than costing everyone their session.

entries.title: Ops alerts can now reach an inbox, not only the dashboard
entries.summary: Operator alerts gain an email channel next to the private Telegram chat. Critical alerts (a leak, a halted payer, a compromised signer) are emailed and pushed every time they fire; warnings reach Telegram once an hour per signature and arrive by email as one hourly digest with counts and the oldest unresolved item, so an inbox is never flooded. Each channel has its own hourly ceiling, so a storm on one never silences the other. The health check now lists which alert channels are wired and flags production as degraded when no one would be told, and a self-test script proves real delivery on every configured channel.

entries.title: Optional one-wallet-per-call payer for the x402 ring
entries.summary: With X402_RING_FRESH_PAYER=true, every paid ring call is signed by a brand-new wallet that is funded for that call and swept to zero afterwards, so each settlement shows up as its own buyer on x402scan and in our accounting.

entries.title: Paid endpoint 402 challenges validate on external x402 directories
entries.summary: The agent-reputation and agent-bouncer challenges no longer carry amount-0 placeholder entries that directory validators rejected. The free Bearer and Sign-In-With-X path still works and is now listed per route in the OpenAPI document and the x402 discovery document.

entries.title: Paying in $THREE from your own wallet works on the marketplace, copy trading and launch funding
entries.summary: When the platform cannot cover the network fee, a marketplace or skill purchase falls back to a transaction your wallet signs and pays for. For a $THREE price that transaction was built for the older token program, so your wallet's safety check refused it before you could approve. The same mistake affected settling a copy-trading fee and funding a launch quoted in $THREE. All of them now read the token program and decimals from the coin itself, open the recipient's $THREE account when it is missing, and send a checked transfer. The agent payment tools fix a run of separate faults. Reading vault balances and changing the buyback split always failed. Distributing payments could not build. Paying an invoice called a method that does not exist. Withdrawing $THREE went to the wrong account. Changing the buyback split from the coin dashboard also failed for every owner. All of these work now, with $THREE vaults read and paid on its own token program.

entries.title: Play holds up on a shaky connection
entries.summary: When the connection drops in Play, you now get a plain explanation and a way forward instead of a raw error code. Builds that fail to save retry on their own until they land, and a world whose saved builds did not load tries again before telling you. A dropped matchmaking poll keeps your community in the war queue. A message thread that fails to load shows a Retry button, and a chat reply that drops shows why instead of "They went quiet". The pay demo only says no funds moved when that is certain. Escape now closes only the top panel, and the loading and error screens, the wheel and the stage prompt follow your language.

entries.title: Pricing and the Forge pay sheet say when a payment option is not switched on yet
entries.summary: The pricing page now asks the server which assets checkout can actually take. Any asset that cannot be paid yet is shown disabled with "Not switched on yet", the $THREE discount is only claimed while $THREE can be paid, and a refused checkout names the asset instead of failing with a generic error. The Forge pay sheet checks the $THREE rail before it opens: when it is not switched on, it says so plainly, asks for no wallet approval and offers no retry loop. Paid Wheel of Fortune spins say the same and point at your free spin. Nothing is charged in any of these states.

entries.title: Seeded catalog assets can now be judged on how they look, not just their structure
entries.summary: Platform-seeded models in /characters and /objects were gated on mesh structure only, because rendering and judging an asset did not fit inside the seed cron's time limit. A new per-minute vision cron now takes assets that pass the mesh check, renders each one and asks the vision judge whether it is realistic, on-prompt and complete, then publishes it or sets it aside with the full verdict for tuning. A judge that is down is retried and never blocks a sound asset for more than 30 minutes. The judge also now falls back across every vision provider instead of depending on one. It switches on with SEED_VISION_PHASE=1 after deploy.

entries.title: Slow phones and laptops now drop to lighter graphics in /play within seconds
entries.summary: /play, the club and the trade room lower their graphics settings when a device can't keep up, but they were measuring frame time in a way that made a device drawing 2 frames a second look like one drawing 20. A struggling phone or older laptop could spend half a minute or more on the heaviest settings before anything changed, and a device below 1 frame a second could stay there for minutes. They now measure the real time between frames, so a device that can't keep up steps down to lighter settings within a couple of seconds, while a healthy device coming back from a hidden tab is left alone.

entries.title: Status page shows the retired world as retired, not down
entries.summary: The deleted world.three.ws service now carries an explicit, reversible retired state: the health rollup, alerts and status page no longer report a permanent false outage, so a red status always means something real.

entries.title: The /play lobby points newcomers somewhere, and its welcome card fits at any zoom
entries.summary: The lobby header now links to the product tour (What is three.ws?) and to the coin launchpad, and Launch a coin is listed in the Build menu, so a first-time visitor who is not ready to drop into a world still has a next step. The first-visit welcome card used to be pushed off the top of the screen at 200% browser zoom, on a phone held sideways, or with longer German text, which hid its Skip button; it now scrolls inside its overlay so every button stays reachable. The card machine, the dance-off tip prompt and the signature wall no longer show raw browser errors such as Failed to fetch or a bare server status: a dropped connection and a struggling server each get one plain line that says what to do, and real explanations from the server are kept.

entries.title: The /play share sheet and network errors behave on keyboards and bad connections
entries.summary: The build share sheet now uses the shared modal stack, so Escape closes only the sheet, Tab stays inside it and focus returns to where you were. Friends, NPC purchases and coin-buy sign-in show a plain network message instead of raw browser text when a connection drops. A new test pins the HUD text colors at WCAG AA contrast over bright and dark scenes.

entries.title: The $THREE Posts chart now runs to today and keeps every post it has ever measured
entries.summary: The Posts view on the $THREE coin page now plots @trythreews posts through November, with all 197 posts measured at +1h, +4h and +24h against the any-time baseline. The price source only serves the last 180 days, so every 15-minute bar read is now archived and merged on each refresh, and the oldest posts keep the returns measured for them earlier instead of going blank.

entries.title: The GTC 2027 poster, its data and its build scripts are in the repository
entries.summary: docs/nvidia-gtc-2027 holds the print-ready 43 by 24 inch poster PDF for the NVIDIA GTC 2027 call for posters, the measured coverage and latency data behind every number on it, the avatar frames rendered by the shipping Audio2Face player, and two npm scripts (poster:gtc:rigs, poster:gtc) that rebuild the sheet and refuse to print a column that overflows. The README carries the submission form copy, and a companion Hugging Face article draft explains the direct and derived blendshape mapping.

entries.title: The predictions scanner reads the markets nearest par and names each one in full
entries.summary: The no-arbitrage scanner on Agent Predictions now spends its order-book reads on the open markets whose YES plus NO price sits closest to par, skips markets whose close time has passed, and honours its market cap even when one event holds hundreds of brackets. Each row now shows the event and the outcome together, and the note under the scanner says how many books were read and how many had both sides quoted.

entries.title: The roadmap now shows where each phase really stands
entries.summary: ROADMAP.md renders correctly again (its status icons had been corrupted) and matches the README roadmap line for line. Phase 2 now says what has shipped: voice preview, the voice library and voice cloning, the persona interview and memory seeding all run in the main creation flow, not only on the demos hub, and the week-2 retention target is measured. Phase 3 notes the economy contracts and their audit pack are built with the external audit next, and Phase 5 shows the macOS and iOS widget is built and waits only on an Apple Developer account.

entries.title: The Solana agent SDK pays in $THREE, confirms every transaction for real, and throws errors you can catch by type
entries.summary: Several fixes in @three-ws/solana-agent for developers building agents on Solana. x402 exact payments now work in Token-2022 tokens such as $THREE on both sides: the paying client builds the transfer under the token's real program and the facilitator verifies it there, so a $THREE payment is no longer impossible, and a payee that is a program address (an escrow or vault) no longer crashes the payer. Plain token transfers can pay those program addresses too. The swap approval prompt reads each token's real decimals from chain, so a 9-decimal Token-2022 coin is no longer shown a thousand times too large, and if a token cannot be read the swap stops instead of showing a guessed figure. Token balance and token list reads cover both token programs. Every send now waits for real confirmation: a transaction that landed but failed throws instead of reporting success, and a send whose blockhash expired stops right away instead of waiting out the full timeout, Jupiter swaps included. Every failure is a named error class (wallet not connected, confirmation timeout, retries exhausted, invalid input, request failed and more) whose name survives the minified build and whose instanceof check works across the package's entry points. The test suite grew from 59 to 238 tests. Reaches npm with the next @three-ws/solana-agent release.

entries.title: three-ws-agent: run your three.ws agent from the terminal
entries.summary: A new command-line agent runs on your own machine or VPS. Sign in with a browser code, then chat in a terminal UI that streams replies, asks before every write, shell, network or wallet action (wallet actions always ask and show recipient, amount, token and chain), and lets you stop or redirect a turn mid-stream. Sessions are saved and searchable, /subagent runs side tasks in parallel, schedules accept plain language such as "every weekday at 9am" and can run on this machine or as a three.ws automation that runs while your computer is off, and gateway mode answers allowlisted Telegram chats. Install it from the repository, with Docker, Nix or the Windows installer.

entries.title: three.ws 3D Studio plugins for Hermes, Cursor and Dify
entries.summary: Three more agent platforms can now make 3D models for free. The Hermes and Cursor plugins connect the agent to the studio MCP server and bundle the generate, avatar, rig and catalog skills. The Dify plugin adds four native tools to Dify agents and workflows: Generate 3D Model, Create 3D Avatar, Rig 3D Model and Search 3D Assets, each returning the GLB link, a viewer link and optionally the GLB file itself. Neither needs a key or an account.

entries.title: three.ws can now be bought through Microsoft Marketplace, Copilot, Teams, Power Platform and the Microsoft Store
entries.summary: The groundwork for selling three.ws through Microsoft is in place. A team that buys a three.ws plan on Microsoft Marketplace lands on /microsoft/activate, signs in with their work account, and gets the same plan a card purchase gives, billed on their Microsoft invoice. Plan changes, suspension and cancellation flow back automatically, and tool calls and agent messages are reported to Microsoft every hour, with Microsoft-side hiccups retried rather than dropped. Alongside it: a Microsoft 365 Copilot agent and Teams app with a bot and a tab, a Power Platform connector with five actions for Power Automate, Power Apps, Logic Apps and Copilot Studio, and a Windows app package for the Microsoft Store, each with a validator. Each one goes live after its Microsoft review.

entries.title: Token holder and security checks now share their Solana reads, cutting RPC calls by about 43%
entries.summary: The holders and security panels read the same mint account and largest-holder list for a token, and a page that shows both used to pay for those reads twice, once per server instance it landed on. Those public reads are now shared across the whole fleet for 30 seconds, and the security verdict for a token is reused for 60 seconds, so a burst of lookups costs a fraction of the calls. If every data source is down, the security check now serves the last good verdict for up to 6 hours, clearly marked as stale, instead of failing. Operators also get a per-route RPC spend board at /api/ops/rpc-spend, a terminal report, and an optional daily budget per RPC lane that keeps the remaining quota for payments and settlements.

entries.title: Trader scores, reviews, model checks and tournament results now land on Solana
entries.summary: Five kinds of on-chain record had been failing on every attempt. The daily trader-score credential, review attestations, GLB validation attestations, tournament podiums and hire attestations each named their subject (the trader wallet or the agent) on the memo instruction without that account signing, and Solana's memo program rejects any account that did not sign. No trader score had ever been recorded on mainnet. The subject now sits on a separate read-only instruction, so each record lands and still shows up under the subject's own transaction history, which is what Trader Passport verification and the reputation crawler rely on. The same fix applies to feedback, task and dispute attestations sent through the @three-ws/sdk browser helpers, which had the same flaw.

entries.title: Turn MCP tool groups on or off yourself at /settings/mcp-tools
entries.summary: When an MCP server refuses a tool because it is switched off, the link in the refusal now opens a real page. Sign in and you see every tool group with its plain description. Set a group to on to unlock all of its tools, including financial ones such as swaps, transfers and launches, or to off to hide it from every connected client. Your choice is saved to your account and applies to every client within about 15 seconds, with no need to reconnect or send a header.

entries.title: Voice rooms and background jobs pick up new keys without a restart
entries.summary: The LiveKit voice-room token and the QStash background-job settings are now read through the same central configuration as every other credential, at request time and with stray whitespace trimmed. A key added to the running service now takes effect on the next request instead of waiting for a fresh instance, and a pasted secret with a trailing newline no longer signs voice-room tokens with the wrong bytes. The master wallet endpoint also stopped creating its own database table on the fly: that table is defined only by its reviewed migration now, so its shape can no longer drift.

entries.title: What three.ws builds with NVIDIA, and the poster we are taking to GTC 2027
entries.summary: A new blog post lays out everything three.ws runs on NVIDIA: thirteen L4 and Blackwell GPU deployments that generated 19,270 3D models in a month, Nemotron, Riva and Magpie through NIM, and an Audio2Face-3D digital human that talks in a browser tab with nothing installed. It explains what NVIDIA Inception membership adds, and previews our application to the GTC 2027 call for posters: one facial animation track that drives 98.1% of real user avatars that have face morphs, from text to a speaking face in a median 3.8 seconds. Inception startups can also claim $25 of three.ws credit on the NVIDIA page.

entries.title: Agent Memory Settings
entries.summary: See, edit and delete everything your agents have learned about you: the about-you profile, saved memories and skills drafted from experience. One switch turns learning off, and a cadence control sets how often agents review what to keep.

entries.title: Coin Control
entries.summary: Run the coin your agent launched: buy back and burn with creator fees, send SOL rewards to holders, pay bounties from the agent wallet, and publish every action with its Solana transaction.

entries.title: Custody Integrity
entries.summary: The platform-wide proof of custody: how many six-hourly Merkle roots over every agent wallet are anchored on Solana, and the newest one re-verified against the chain in your browser, no account needed.

entries.title: Docs · Agent memory and learning
entries.summary: What your agents remember, the about-you profile and skills they draft from experience, the owner controls to edit, delete or turn learning off, the privacy guarantees on sale, and the /api/memory routes.

entries.title: Docs · Coin Control
entries.summary: How Coin Control turns an agent coin's creator fees into confirmed buybacks, on-chain burns, SOL rewards to holders and bounties, and publishes each with its Solana transaction.

entries.title: Docs · NVIDIA Inception member perk
entries.summary: How NVIDIA Inception startups apply for $25 of prepaid three.ws credit and earn $10 more for a public shoutout, why a person reviews each one, and how both grants flow through the credit ledger.

entries.title: 3D scenes across the site now use studio lighting and come back on their own after a graphics driver reset
entries.summary: Nineteen 3D pages and previews that drew their own scenes, including the live agent economy, /stream, the haunted yard, the pumpkin carver, the pill, the timeline, the Agora model viewer and the motion tools, now light models with a soft studio environment. Metal, glossy plastic and skin pick up highlights instead of rendering flat or dark. Those scenes also pause when you scroll them offscreen or switch tabs, which saves battery. Every embedded avatar now lowers its resolution slightly when your device starts dropping frames, then raises it again when there is headroom. If the graphics driver resets, the scene shows a short notice and returns by itself, so you no longer need to reload the page.

entries.title: A GitHub Release every week
entries.summary: The three.ws repository now gets a release every Monday, listing what shipped that week in plain language, so anyone watching or starring the repo sees steady progress in their GitHub feed.

entries.title: A VRoid Hub character keeps its creator's license after you import it
entries.summary: Importing from VRoid Hub now records the creator's license on the avatar and enforces it everywhere: a character whose creator withholds public agents cannot be put on an agent, one that disallows redistribution cannot be made public, pinned to IPFS, sold or minted, and one that disallows modification cannot be restyled, replaced or regenerated. Each refusal names the creator. Forking cannot launder the license, the creator's credit and Hub link show on the avatar and agent pages, and the creator's own characters have every action open.

entries.title: A withdrawal that fails after it was sent can no longer be paid twice
entries.summary: Payouts now record the signed transaction before it is broadcast. If the send errors or times out afterwards, the withdrawal shows as confirming and keeps your balance held instead of failing and freeing it, and the payout cron settles it from the chain: completed when it landed, failed only when it provably never can. Operators are paged if one stays unconfirmed for more than 30 minutes.

entries.title: Add three.ws to your coding agent in one line, and read the README in Chinese, Japanese or Korean
entries.summary: The top of the three.ws GitHub page now shows a one-command install for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, plus live counts of models forged and agents created. Free text to 3D and rigged avatars work straight away, with no key and no account. The README also has a How it works diagram, a plain note on what is free and what costs money, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean translations, and a place to show what you built. For just the 3D tools, the new three-ws-3d-skills repository packages six 3D skills you can install on their own.

entries.title: An open head unit: your agent beside CarPlay or Android Auto
entries.summary: A new open-source head unit app puts a real CarPlay or Android Auto session on one half of a car screen and the three.ws Drive agent on the other, on a Raspberry Pi or any Linux box with a Carlinkit CPC200 dongle. With no dongle plugged in it says so plainly and shows the USB ids it is looking for. It is built and tested up to the USB port; the first run on real hardware is next. Drive also stops asking for your own agents when you are signed out, so a fresh head unit or phone loads the public agents without an error.

entries.title: Cinematic and Portrait looks get real contact shadows
entries.summary: The Cinematic and Portrait looks in the 3D viewer now use N8AO ambient occlusion, the same denoised technique the /play world runs. Creases, armpits, joints and the space between limbs pick up soft contact shading that the previous effect barely showed. The shading scales with the model, so tiny figurines and full-size avatars look equally grounded, and there is a new AO radius slider in the Cinematic FX panel. The default Studio look is unchanged and never downloads the extra code.

entries.title: Codespaces, a roadmap page, a support page and categorized release notes
entries.summary: One-click GitHub Codespaces (dev container), ROADMAP.md, SUPPORT.md and categorized GitHub release notes landed for contributors and new visitors. The README also gained copy-paste MCP install blocks for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Windsurf.

entries.title: Coin Control: buy back, burn and reward holders with your coin's creator fees
entries.summary: Creators can now put the fees their agent's coin earns to work from one page. Set a rule to buy back and burn the coin each period (the burn uses exactly what the buy returned, read from the confirmed transaction), send SOL to the top holders split by size or by a lottery anyone can re-check, and post bounties paid from the agent wallet. Nothing runs until you confirm the exact terms, every send passes your spend limits, and every action appears with its Solana transaction on a public page holders can open, next to your verified X handle.

entries.title: Coin intel, the launcher and reputation are updating again
entries.summary: For a stretch of 3 November the database sat past its storage mark, and the background jobs that refresh coin intel, the launcher feed, smart-money rollups and wallet reputation paused rather than risk filling it. They are running again. The real cause was seven big history tables (on-chain agent events, oracle training rows, the settlement log, firewall decisions, usage events, sniper verdicts and ops alerts) that nothing ever trimmed. Their older rows are now copied to cold storage on Google Cloud, checked against a fingerprint, and only then removed from the live database, so nothing is lost and any month can be restored. Rows that are still needed stay put: billing records, coins still waiting for a label, and alerts nobody has acknowledged. Lifetime settlement totals on the x402 ring keep counting pruned days through a daily rollup, so the published numbers never shrink. The platform health check now reports database storage and raises an alert at 75 percent of the mark, well before anything pauses.

entries.title: Editable parts engines are ready to switch on, with a commercially licensed background cutter
entries.summary: The two engines behind Editable parts (PartCrafter, which turns one photo into separately named parts, and HoloPart, which fills in the hidden side of each part) now build cleanly with every self-check passing, and their model weights are already in place on our own storage. PartCrafter's original background-removal step relied on a model licensed for non-commercial use only, so it now uses BiRefNet (MIT) instead, running on the same GPU. A real photo has been turned into named parts end to end. Both engines go live with the next owner-approved deploy.

entries.title: Every partner logo now sits in the site footer
entries.summary: The footer on every page carries a Partners and programs row with all nine partners from the partners page: OpenAI, IBM, Microsoft, AWS, Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, NVIDIA, HackerNoon and Quicknode. Each logo opens that partner's page, and an All partners link opens the full directory. The footer mascot now stands above the row instead of drifting over the logos on phones.

entries.title: Exit fills show their reason again, and 3D workers refuse files that point off the payload
entries.summary: When a trailing-ratchet order sold on a lock tier or a drawdown, the fill in your agent wallet's order history lost the reason chip that says why it sold. It is back on every exit fill. The 3D mesh workers (remesh, rig, segment, stylize, texture and the others that decode compressed models) now reject a glTF whose buffers or images point at files outside the upload itself, before any decoder reads them. On the HQ events map, tech events in San Jose and Cambridge now land in California and Massachusetts instead of Costa Rica and England.

entries.title: Forged items in /play land where you place their hologram
entries.summary: Forging an item inside a /play world now gives you a hologram to place straight away. It shows the real forge progress above it with a Cancel button, and when the model is ready it materializes on that exact spot for everyone in the server. If a forge fails, the hologram becomes a marker with the reason, Retry and Dismiss, and nothing comes out of your build budget. Forged models are held to a size ceiling that suits your device (phones get a lighter one), oversized results are simplified automatically, and the world itself refuses models it cannot load or that are too large. The Forge form lists what you made this session and gives an honest wait: about 90 seconds usually, up to 6 minutes when the lane is busy.

entries.title: LiveKit avatars keep playing for visitors without a microphone
entries.summary: An <agent-3d voice="livekit"> embed used to report a failed connection whenever the visitor had no microphone or said no to the permission prompt, even though the room was joined and the avatar was already talking. It now joins in listen-only mode: the agent's voice plays and the avatar keeps lip-syncing and gesturing. Visitors who do have a microphone can still talk back.

entries.title: My cards reaches every card in a big wallet, with search
entries.summary: The My cards view of the /play card gacha used to stop at the first 120 cards. It now lists the whole wallet 60 cards at a time in name order, with a Show more button that keeps your place, and a search box that looks through every card in the wallet by name, year, set number or grade. A search for "psa 10" returns only grade 10 cards. Cards you can sell back right now are gathered in a Sellable now section at the top, and every card on screen gets its buyback price checked, not just the first 60. Opening My cards while the machine list was still loading no longer gets replaced by that list.

entries.title: My cards shows every card's photo, grade and value again
entries.summary: In production the My cards view of the /play card gacha listed cards with blank photos and no grade or value, and sometimes failed to load at all. Card details now load from a backup Arweave gateway when the main one is busy, and the wallet scan uses the platform's full set of Solana providers instead of the public node alone. Other pages that read Arweave files (agent cards, token details) also skip two gateways that had stopped answering.

entries.title: Operators can extend, rename or end the live event without a deploy
entries.summary: A new authed override, set with npm run event:override or POST /api/event-config, changes the live event's window or name on top of the baked-in schedule. The countdown, the event leaderboard and the game server's quest gate all follow it within about a minute, and fall back to the static schedule if the API is unreachable. Every change is validated with the same rules as the deploy gate and audit-logged.

entries.title: Pages fit a phone screen, and small buttons are easier to tap
entries.summary: A full-site pass at phone width fixed layouts that were wider than the screen and got cut off on the right: examples, data desk, diorama, herald, assistant, splat, bazaar, markets, crypto, developers, ship, materialize, go, leaderboard, the arena, trades and news. Long addresses and links now wrap instead of pushing the column wide. On touch screens, the docs Run and Edit buttons, the docs freshness link, tutorial Copy buttons, disclosure rows, and controls on character library, prompts, yields, guards, live agents, everything, exchanges, ship and forged now have a full 44px tap area.

entries.title: Path-traced stills of any model or avatar, straight from the viewer
entries.summary: The 3D viewer can now render a physically based still of exactly what you are looking at: real soft shadows, colour bleeding between surfaces and reflections that see the rest of the scene, computed by a GPU path tracer rather than approximated. Press Shift+P or choose Path-traced render in the Display panel, watch the image converge on the canvas with a progress bar and Cancel, and the finished PNG downloads. Developers get the same render from the agent-3d element with renderPhotoreal() and from iframe embeds with the renderPhotoreal bridge action. The path tracer loads only when you ask for a render, so pages that never use it are no heavier.

entries.title: Playground tabs, competition retry and 3D clean-up passes work again
entries.summary: A sweep of broken controls across the site. The API playground on the classic homepage switches to its Node SDK and cURL tabs again (a duplicated id had bound them to the embed playground instead), and the launcher's payment rail picker responds to clicks. The Retry button on the competitions page now reloads agents when the first load fails. The /grok and /connect pages lost sections that a merge had rendered twice. Trading tools report a quote router outage plainly instead of calling a busy market thin, and the onchain viewer moves to a backup Solana RPC when one stalls. In the 3D worker, the decimate and repair clean-up passes run again, and their output now stays with the job so long sessions no longer fill the worker's memory with leftover meshes. Agent templates and persona interviews in the create wizard are now counted in analytics.

entries.title: Proof of custody anchors on Solana mainnet again
entries.summary: The six-hourly custody Merkle root is now committed as a signed SPL-Memo on mainnet, where the attester wallet is funded, instead of an unfunded devnet payer that rejected all 524 earlier anchors. A failed anchor now pages ops once per outage with the attester and its balance, an unfunded payer is recorded as attester_unfunded:<network>, and the public integrity page returns showing anchored versus total epochs, with an honest banner when the latest epoch is not yet anchored.

entries.title: Rejoining /play after a dropped connection puts you back where you stood
entries.summary: A player whose connection dropped now comes back at the spot they left instead of frozen at spawn, and the world shows no ghost copy of them. Players in voice chat who mute now show a muted marker to everyone else, a long unbroken chat line such as a pasted address wraps inside the speech bubble, and a boutique purchase can only be started once while the wallet is signing, so a second click never opens a second $THREE payment. Event jobs stay closed outside the live window, including when the event config cannot be reached.

entries.title: See, edit and delete everything your agents have learned about you
entries.summary: A new Agent memory page lists the profile your agents keep about you, every memory they saved and the skills they drafted from experience. Edit or delete any line with an undo, turn learning off with one switch, set how often agents review what to keep, and review drafted skills with a diff, version history and rollback. A marketplace transfer now also deletes an agent's drafted skills and session summaries.

entries.title: Smoother edges on every 3D model and avatar viewer
entries.summary: Models shown on a solid or studio background, which covers most embeds, the Forge result viewer and avatar pages, now have antialiased edges. The post-processing that adds the soft glow and vignette was drawing into a buffer that skipped the browser's edge smoothing, so outlines, fingers and hair stair-stepped. Edges are now smoothed with four samples (two on low-power phones) and the overall look is unchanged.

entries.title: Text to 3D no longer fails with "Mesh missed" when a GPU worker is busy
entries.summary: One slow GPU worker could trip a shared safety breaker and make every other 3D lane report as unreachable for 30 seconds at a time. Each worker now has its own breaker, and status checks no longer block new jobs, so a generation that is queued behind a busy worker is accepted instead of being rejected.

entries.title: The /play world holds up better for Meetup #3: lost connections, screen readers and Safari
entries.summary: Ahead of Community Meetup #3 we audited the /play world on phones, in Safari and with a keyboard and screen reader, and fixed what we found. When your connection drops, chat you typed stays in the box, party invites and party chat tell you they were not sent, the Jobs Board says the room is offline instead of loading forever, and paid shop and wheel purchases are resent once you reconnect rather than left hanging. The sign-in gate now says when the community service is unreachable instead of showing "Failed to fetch". Escape closes the top panel every time, gold and cash changes are read out to screen readers, typing in a field no longer triggers shortcuts, and nameplates and damage numbers sit on a dark backing so they stay readable over a bright scene. The signature wall retries if its first load fails, Safari no longer logs a connection error on every join, and the trending coin board keeps showing coins when its upstream source is unavailable.

entries.title: The $THREE balance gate now fails closed during an RPC outage
entries.summary: Agents that require a minimum $THREE balance for a paid skill used to let every caller through whenever the Solana RPC was unhealthy. The balance check now retries once and, if the balance still cannot be read, answers 503 and asks the caller to retry. A paid skill call in that state does not consume the payment. The public balance endpoint answers 503 rpc_unavailable instead of a false eligible: true.

entries.title: The 3D viewer and <agent-3d> can now render on WebGPU
entries.summary: Add ?renderer=webgpu to /app, or renderer="webgpu" to an <agent-3d> embed, to draw the avatar on WebGPU with the full cinematic look (ambient occlusion, depth of field, bloom, color grade, grain, vignette) rebuilt on three's node pipeline. Every preset and Cinematic FX slider works the same on both paths. Without a WebGPU adapter, or if the GPU is lost mid-session, the viewer drops to WebGL2 on its own and keeps the scene. VRM toon materials are converted so VRM avatars render on WebGPU too. The default stays WebGL2. Preset sliders in the Cinematic FX panel also stay in sync after switching presets.

entries.title: The A3S streaming avatar no longer turns into jagged shards as it refines
entries.summary: On the streaming avatar comparison page the A3S panel showed the right avatar for a moment, then collapsed into garbled, spiky geometry as the finer layers arrived, and sometimes blanked with a console error. The refinement step copied the wrong bytes out of the coarse model it was growing, so the original vertices were scrambled. It now reads those vertices correctly and refreshes the cached bounds, so the avatar sharpens in place and ends identical to the classic panel.

entries.title: The classic homepage avatar now shows head to toe, and appears on phones
entries.summary: On the classic homepage, the animation buttons used to cover the live avatar's feet, so the figure looked like it was floating. It now stands above the buttons with its feet and ground shadow in view. On phones the avatar area had collapsed to nothing, so mobile visitors never saw the live 3D agent at all. It now appears below the headline at a comfortable height.

entries.title: The live agent economy stage shows two idling avatars on their pedestals
entries.summary: On the live agent economy page both avatars stood in a stiff arms-out T-pose inside dark boxes that hid the stage, with a webcam and emote toolbar showing and the avatars floating above their pedestals. Avatar embeds now start their idle animation by default and honor the chrome-free overlay setting, the transparent background no longer paints an opaque box, the avatars stand on their pedestals, and the central screen's text is readable.

entries.title: The service catalog AI agents read to find three.ws loads in about a second
entries.summary: The public catalog that AI agents and directories read to discover three.ws paid services could take 20 to 30 seconds to load, often enough for a crawler to give up. It now always answers from the most recent copy while a fresh one is built in the background, and it fetches its market data sources at the same time instead of one by one.

entries.title: The x402 payment audit ledger no longer drops or double-writes rows
entries.summary: A payment audit row that fails to write or times out now moves to a dead-letter list and is retried with backoff instead of being discarded, and after ten failures it is parked in a table for review. A replayed event is stored once, enforced by a unique index on transaction hash and event type. Ops is paged when the dead-letter stays non-empty for 15 minutes, and the money-health board shows its depth. Audit retention is configurable and every row is archived to object storage, and verified, before it is deleted.

entries.title: Turn a photo into a Gaussian splat right in the Splat Viewer
entries.summary: The Splat Viewer has a new Generate from a photo card. Drop in a PNG, JPG or WebP (or paste an image link), pick Light, Balanced or Maximum detail, and a GPU running TripoSplat builds a photoreal splat of the object. The card shows each real step with the elapsed time, can be cancelled, and loads the result straight into the stage as a shareable link, ready for hotspots, the camera path and video export. If something goes wrong it says what, in plain words: a photo that is too big, uploads being down, the lane not being switched on, or the GPU rejecting the image. The first run after a quiet spell takes a few minutes while the GPU warms up; after that, about a minute.

entries.title: Viewer screenshots capture the model instead of a blank frame
entries.summary: Pressing P or choosing Screenshot in the 3D viewer could save an empty image with only the watermark on it. The viewer drew the frame, then waited for the watermark to download, and by then the browser had already cleared the canvas. It now has the watermark ready before it draws, so the saved PNG always shows the model you were looking at.

entries.title: A lock screen worth stopping at
entries.summary: The desktop's lock screen now shows your own wallpaper behind it, like a real OS, instead of a flat black void. A portrait of the avatar you walk in as replaces the question-mark badge, a live status light shows whether every system came up, and the $THREE chip turns green or red with the day's move. New destination tiles let you skip the walk and arrive straight at your workstation, the Exchange, the Launchpad, the Mine, the Forge, the Gallery, the Agent Plaza or the Marketplace.

entries.title: Card gacha: a 3D capsule reveal, My cards, and selling from your wallet
entries.summary: Pulling a card in /play now plays a full 3D reveal: the capsule spins and shakes as light gathers into it, then cracks open with a flash, a shockwave and a light pillar in the card's rarity colour, and the real graded slab spins out with a holographic foil that shifts as you turn it. Rare and epic pulls hide their colour until the last second. A new My cards button lists every Collector Crypt card in your wallet with its grade, insured value and real front and back photos, lets you inspect each one in 3D, and sells a card back for USDC while its 72 hour buyback is open, behind a confirmation table and a stricter transaction check that refuses anything but the one card leaving your wallet.

entries.title: NVIDIA Inception badge on the homepage
entries.summary: The homepage now shows the NVIDIA Inception member badge in its footer and lists NVIDIA Inception in the partner strip, both linking to the NVIDIA page. Every other page already carries the badge through the shared footer.

entries.title: three.ws dresses for autumn
entries.summary: Halloween is over, so the site has changed into its fall colours through the end of November. The desktop has a new Harvest wallpaper of a valley at golden hour with leaves drifting down, an amber accent, and a matching lock screen. The classic homepage gets falling maple leaves, autumn prompt ideas for the Forge, and a Leaf pile button that makes the avatar jump into the leaves. Harvest stays in your wallpaper list for good, and you can switch the look off any time in Settings, Personalization.

entries.title: three.ws is up for review in NVIDIA's startup app catalog
entries.summary: Our product record, three.ws 3D AI Studio, is filed with NVIDIA Inception for its catalog of apps from member startups. It lists the NVIDIA technology three.ws runs in production today (CUDA, cuDNN, Kaolin, Riva voice and Audio2Face facial animation) and keeps what we are only evaluating separate. On November 2 we followed up with the Inception team to confirm the record is complete and ask when the next review runs. NVIDIA curates the catalog, so we are not listed yet. We will post here the day we are.

entries.title: Docs · Dance-off rounds in /play
entries.summary: How a /play dance-off runs: the server round machine, how a crowd reaction becomes a vote, tie and leaver rules, the Spotlight Champion aura, the cadence during and outside an event, and the confirm-first tip card.

entries.title: Docs · Parties in /play
entries.summary: How /play parties work: invites, the 8 member cap, party chat, safe same-world teleports and cross-world handoff, member identity across reconnects, and the store keys and TTLs behind it.

entries.title: Docs · The /play activity ticker and hype moments
entries.summary: What feeds the /play activity ticker, how each coin learns its own big-buy threshold, the cooldown that keeps hype moments rare, and the trade tape fallback when the primary feed is blocked.

entries.title: Docs · The /play venue projector view
entries.summary: How /play?director=1 turns a browser into an unattended venue screen: an invisible spectator seat, an auto-director camera that cuts between occupied landmarks, a projector-scale broadcast overlay with the presenter PA lower third, and the resilience that keeps it running all event.

entries.title: Docs · The $THREE signature wall
entries.summary: How the /play signature wall works: one signature per wallet or guest session, the filters and rate limit on writes, live propagation to the room, density paging that stays legible at thousands of names, the share cards, and how to moderate it.

entries.title: Docs · The card gacha machine in /play
entries.summary: How to pull a real graded trading card from the capsule machine on the /play plaza, the 3D reveal, viewing and selling the cards in your wallet, what the transaction checks prove before you sign, and the /api/gacha routes.

entries.title: A card gacha machine in /play: pull real graded trading cards
entries.summary: A capsule vending machine now stands on the west plaza of every /play world. Walk up and press E to browse Collector Crypt's live machines with their odds, stock, recent winners and the cards still inside, then pull a professionally graded, vaulted card for USDC straight from your own Solana wallet. Before you sign, you see exactly what the payment does, checked against the real transaction. The machine cranks out a capsule and the card flips over in its rarity colour, with a link to verify the pull was fair. Keep the card, or sell it back within 72 hours.

entries.title: A live activity ticker and big-buy hype moments in /play
entries.summary: /play now has a small collapsible feed of joins, leaves, trades, wheel wins, cosmetic unlocks and your quest completions. When a genuinely large buy lands for the coin, measured against that coin's own recent trades, the world gets a gold hype moment, a jumbotron banner and an optional chime. The $THREE trade tape also keeps working when the primary trade feed is blocked, by falling back to the pool's trades.

entries.title: Dance-off rounds on the /play dance floor
entries.summary: Dancers on the floor now compete in timed rounds judged by the crowd's reactions, one counted vote per person per round. The winner gets a spotlight, confetti, a jumbotron feature with their name and avatar, and a free Spotlight Champion aura. Rounds run every few minutes during the meetup and can be started by anyone on the floor.

entries.title: Display settings opens the right page
entries.summary: Right-clicking the web desktop and choosing Display settings opened the same Personalization page as Personalize. It now opens Desktop and taskbar, where icon size, icon layout and the taskbar live.

entries.title: Move desktop widgets with the keyboard
entries.summary: Desktop widgets could only be rearranged by dragging. In edit mode (right-click the desktop, Edit widgets) you can now focus a widget and press an arrow key to move it one cell, hopping over any widget in the way. Screen readers hear where it landed, the new spot is saved like a drag, and a hint on the edit bar says how.

entries.title: Parties in /play: team up with up to 8 players
entries.summary: Invite anyone from their inspect panel or your friends list and stay together across the world. Party members get a sky-blue nameplate accent, minimap blips, screen-edge chips for members out of range, a private party chat (or /p from any scope), and a Go to button that drops you safely beside a member, or hands you off to their coin's world with the party intact.

entries.title: Sign the wall: a permanent $THREE signature wall in the /play world
entries.summary: A graffiti wall near spawn where every visitor can sign once with a name and an 80-character line. New signatures appear live for everyone in the room with an ink splash, the wall stays readable from 10 to thousands of signatures by paging through them, and every signature has its own shareable card.

entries.title: Task Manager reads cleanly on a phone
entries.summary: On a phone the desktop Task Manager broke window sizes and the Memory heading across two lines. Every value and heading now stays on one line and only a long app name shortens.

entries.title: Halloween Weekend Gifts
entries.summary: Free Halloween gifts, claimable October 31 to November 1, 2026 only: a 3D Pumpkin Cap and the Witchlight aura for /play, a permanent profile badge and a haunted desktop wallpaper. Claim once, keep forever.

entries.title: Haunted Graveyard
entries.summary: Walk a moonlit 3D graveyard in your browser: a crypt, fenced yard, flickering lamps and pumpkins, and a zombie, skeleton, vampire, ghost and keeper you can click, follow and make dance. Built from Kenney's CC0 Graveyard Kit.

entries.title: How pumpkin carving works
entries.summary: The /pumpkin carver: a hollow ribbed 3D shell, real boolean cuts with three-bvh-csg, the knife, undo, saved cuts, and PNG and GLB export.

entries.title: How seasonal drops work
entries.summary: Free, time-boxed gifts on three.ws: one claim during the window grants a profile badge, /play wearables and a desktop wallpaper you keep forever. The window, the /api/seasonal endpoint, the seasonal look and its opt-out, and how to add the next drop.

entries.title: How the haunted graveyard works
entries.summary: The /haunted page: Kenney's CC0 Graveyard Kit ingested into the object library, the deterministic yard layout, the five animated characters, and how to publish the models to the CDN.

entries.title: Pumpkin Carving
entries.summary: Carve a real 3D pumpkin in your browser: boolean cuts through a hollow ribbed shell, six stamp shapes, a freehand knife, a flickering candle that shines through your design, undo, and PNG or GLB export.

entries.title: /play gets contact shadows and glow on capable devices
entries.summary: On high-quality devices, /play now renders with ambient occlusion (props and avatars ground into the world), a soft bloom on bright and emissive things like the Witchlight aura, and filmic tone mapping. It switches itself off in power-saver mode and on lower quality tiers, and falls back to the plain renderer if the GPU cannot run it.

entries.title: 91 free Halloween 3D models join the object library, and you can walk them in a haunted graveyard
entries.summary: Kenney's Graveyard Kit (CC0, free for any use) is now in the object library: crypts, gravestones, fences, lampposts, pumpkins, trees and five animated characters (a zombie, skeleton, vampire, ghost and graveyard keeper), each one a single self-contained GLB. The new /haunted page puts them together as a moonlit 3D yard you can orbit, light, photograph and populate with wandering monsters.

entries.title: A venue screen for /play: an invisible camera that directs itself
entries.summary: Open /play with director=1 on a projector or as an OBS source and the world watches itself. The screen joins as a spectator that has no avatar, is invisible to every player and is not counted in the online total, then cuts every 15 to 30 seconds between the busiest places in the plaza (the totem, the screens, the dance floor, any crowd) without ever clipping a building. A broadcast overlay shows the event name with LIVE or a countdown, the running agenda item, the world and the live headcount, and a QR to join, with no player HUD. At the group photo it holds the totem and the crowd through the countdown and the flash. It reconnects forever under a quiet pill, keeps the screen awake, hides the cursor, and reloads itself if graphics are lost. Built for the Meetup #3 livestream.

entries.title: Carve a 3D pumpkin at /pumpkin
entries.summary: A new pumpkin carver lets you cut a real hollow 3D pumpkin in your browser. Stamp round, triangle, square, star, moon or bat shapes, drag the knife for freehand lines, resize and rotate each cut, then light the candle to watch it glow and throw light through your design. Undo works per cut, your pumpkin is remembered between visits, and you can save a picture or download the carved pumpkin as a GLB. The Halloween gifts page now links to it.

entries.title: Chat keeps answering when the free model quota runs out
entries.summary: When the shared free model hit its daily limit, the chat showed 'The built-in model is rate-limited' and stopped. It now hands the message to the platform's own model chain instead, so a reply still arrives. The rate-limit notice only appears if every lane is busy.

entries.title: Desktop list widgets fill their cards
entries.summary: The Pulse, Launches and Agents widgets on the web desktop showed a fixed number of rows and left an empty band at the bottom of the card. They now show as many whole rows as the card has room for, at any widget size or text scale, and never a row cut in half.

entries.title: Desktop notifications show a small app icon again
entries.summary: On the web desktop, a notification's app icon stretched into a wide empty bar across the card header, both in the pop-up and in the notification centre. It is a small square beside the app name again, and a browser test keeps it that way.

entries.title: Desktop windows open without a zoom when reduced motion is on
entries.summary: With your system set to reduce motion, a new window on the web desktop now appears at its full size in place. Before, its first frame still flashed in at 94% scale and slightly low before snapping to size. Closing already skipped its animation; opening now matches. The desktop also has a browser test suite that boots it, opens every built-in app, exercises window controls, saves a file and checks accessibility in dark and light mode.

entries.title: File Explorer fits a phone screen
entries.summary: On a phone the desktop's File Explorer squeezed its address bar down to a single letter and pushed the view buttons off the edge of a toolbar that could only be scrolled sideways. The address bar now gets the room and always shows the folder you are in, the commands go icon-only, item commands that do not apply to your selection step aside, and the toolbar wraps instead of hiding anything.

entries.title: Game-Ready export gets an Artist mesh option for cleaner low-poly
entries.summary: The Game-Ready panel has a new Artist mesh topology: a generative retopology model (LATO.2, MIT) that builds an even low-poly mesh of up to about 10,000 faces. Every result is checked for holes and drift from your model, and if the check fails you automatically get the QuadriFlow mesh instead, so an export never ships torn.

entries.title: Glowing jack-o'-lanterns in /play, and a crowd that walks around each other
entries.summary: During Halloween Weekend, /play worlds are dotted with carved, glowing jack-o'-lanterns (drawn as a few instanced batches, so they stay cheap). The ambient crowd now uses steering behaviours: wanderers arrive smoothly at their destination and keep a body's width from each other instead of walking through one another.

entries.title: Halloween Weekend gets open-source spooky effects: cobwebs, a flying witch, a dropping spider and claim confetti
entries.summary: The classic homepage and /halloween now run halloween.js, a tiny MIT-licensed library, for corner cobwebs, blinking eyes in the dark, a witch crossing the sky, a spider that drops and climbs back up, and a rising tombstone. Claiming your four gifts now sets off an orange and violet confetti burst from canvas-confetti. Both load only during the weekend, respect reduced motion, and switch off with the Halloween look toggle in Settings, Personalization, Season.

entries.title: Halloween Weekend gifts are claimable on /play
entries.summary: The /play lobby now shows the Halloween Weekend 2026 drop with a live countdown, the gift list and a one-click claim for the Pumpkin Cap and Witchlight Aura. A pill follows you into the world until you claim, and a moonlit vignette dresses /play for the weekend (toggle it off with the Halloween look button).
